body.statement:
Under the observed-law conditions and the simultaneous conditional-parallel-trends condition on the baseline-treatment support \(X_0\), the bounded-slope/Lipschitz completion class \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is nonempty if and only if \(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\). Whenever these sets are nonempty,
\[
\{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\}=\Theta(P).
\]
For every \(u\in\mathcal C_P\), the affine one-argument static-schedule lift produces \(Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P)\), preserves the entire joint law \(P\), satisfies \(m_{Q_u}=u\in C(X_0)\), and makes both period schedules individually \(K\)-Lipschitz. Moreover, on one common full-probability event,
\[
Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X)\qquad\text{for every }d\in I,
\]
so the lift satisfies the stronger all-\(I\) parallel-trends equality and \(\theta(Q_u)=\{T-J_P(u)\}/A\). This theorem does not require marginal quasi-stayers. Its model is not the class defined by Assumptions 1--4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024): the theorem additionally imposes the finite \(K\) conditional mean-movement bound, bounded globally \(L\)-Lipschitz baseline trends, continuity of the observed regression version \(g\), and the simultaneous diagonal clause in parallel trends. Thus no equality or global inclusion of the two observed-law models is asserted. On an observed law that satisfies the published assumptions, \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is only the restricted slice satisfying these extra conditions, and \(\Theta(P)\) is not asserted to be the published-class identified set. The result is a sharp bounded-slope/Lipschitz sensitivity repair after failure of the published singleton claim, not a sharp characterization of the unrestricted published class.
body.proof_tex:
By \(\text{ass:compact-treatment}\), \(D_1,D_2\in I\) almost surely, and hence
\[
 |Z|=|D_2-D_1|\leq \operatorname{diam}(I)
 \qquad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
By \(\text{ass:no-stayers}\), \(|Z|>0\) almost surely.  Consequently
\[
 0<A=E_P|Z|\leq \operatorname{diam}(I)<\infty.
\]
Moreover, \(\text{ass:observed-integrability}\) gives
\(E_P|\Delta Y|\leq E_P(|Y_1|+|Y_2|)<\infty\).  Since
\(|S|=1\) almost surely under the no-stayer condition, the definition of \(T\)
therefore gives \(|T|<\infty\).  Thus every ratio below is well defined.

First take \(Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\), where \(\mathfrak Q(P)\) is the class in
\(\text{def:legal-completion-class}\), and write \(m=m_Q\).  Consistency, which
is one of the defining conditions of that class, implies
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Delta Y
 &=Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\\
 &=\{Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\}
   +\{Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The simultaneous clause in \(\text{ass:conditional-parallel-trends}\) supplies
one \(Q\)-full event on which the asserted conditional-mean equality holds for
every \(d\in X_0\).  Since \(D_1=X\in X_0\) almost surely by the definition of
\(X_0\), evaluating the jointly measurable versions on the random diagonal
\(d=X\) is legitimate and yields
\[
 E_Q\!\left[Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\mid X,Z\right]
 =E_Q\!\left[Y_2^Q(X)-Y_1^Q(X)\mid X\right]
 =m(X).
\]
Taking conditional expectations in the preceding decomposition, using the
observed-law match in \(\text{def:legal-completion-class}\), and using the
declared support version \(g\), gives
\[
 g(x,z)-m(x)
 =E_Q\!\left[Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\mid X=x,Z=z\right]
\]
for \(P_{XZ}\)-almost every \((x,z)\).  The condition
\(\text{ass:mean-movement-bound}\) therefore implies
\[
 |g(x,z)-m(x)|\leq K|z|
 \qquad P_{XZ}\text{-almost everywhere}.
\]
The map \((x,z)\mapsto |g(x,z)-m(x)|-K|z|\) is continuous on \(H\): continuity
of \(g\) follows from \(\text{ass:continuous-regression}\), while
\(m\in C(X_0)\) is part of \(\text{def:legal-completion-class}\).  If this map
were positive at a point of \(H=\operatorname{supp}_P(X,Z)\), continuity would
make it positive on a relatively open neighborhood of that point, and the
definition of support would give that neighborhood positive \(P_{XZ}\)-mass.
This would contradict the almost-everywhere inequality.  Hence
\[
 |g(x,z)-m(x)|\leq K|z|
 \qquad\text{for every }(x,z)\in H.
\]
The trend bound and the global \(L\)-Lipschitz condition are also defining
conditions of \(\mathfrak Q(P)\).  Comparing these three properties with
\(\text{def:feasible-trend-class}\) proves \(m\in\mathcal C_P\), and in
particular
\[
 \mathfrak Q(P)\neq\varnothing\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing.
\]

The same decomposition relates the causal estimand to the observed law rather
than defining that relationship.  By the definition of \(\theta(Q)\), the
diagonal conditional-mean equality just established, iterated expectations,
and \(\text{def:signed-functional}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 A\theta(Q)
 &=E_Q\!\left[S\{Y_2^Q(D_2)-Y_2^Q(D_1)\}\right]\\
 &=E_P[S\Delta Y]
   -E_Q\!\left[S\{Y_2^Q(D_1)-Y_1^Q(D_1)\}\right]\\
 &=T-E_P[Sm(X)]\\
 &=T-\int_{X_0}m(x)\,d\nu_P(x)\\
 &=T-J_P(m).
\end{aligned}
\]
The signed integral is finite because \(m\) is bounded and \(\nu_P\) is a
finite signed measure.  Since \(m\in\mathcal C_P\),
\(\text{def:waoss-set}\) now shows
\[
 \{\theta(Q):Q\in\mathfrak Q(P)\}\subseteq\Theta(P).
\]

For the reverse inclusion, fix an arbitrary \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).  Retain on
the same probability space the observed vector with law \(P\), and use the
construction in \(\text{def:affine-lift}\): on \(\{Z\neq0\}\), set
\[
 b_u=\frac{g(X,Z)-u(X)}{Z},
\]
and set \(b_u=0\) on the \(P\)-null event \(\{Z=0\}\).  The variables involved
are Borel measurable because \(g\) and \(u\) are continuous on their compact
supports.  The support obstacle in \(\text{def:feasible-trend-class}\) gives
\[
 |b_u|\leq K\qquad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
Define, simultaneously for every \(d\in I\),
\[
 Y_1^{Q_u}(d)=Y_1+b_u(d-D_1),
 \qquad
 Y_2^{Q_u}(d)=Y_2+b_u(d-D_2).
\]
These are jointly measurable one-argument static schedules.  At the realized
treatments they satisfy, pointwise,
\[
 Y_1^{Q_u}(D_1)=Y_1,
 \qquad
 Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)=Y_2.
\]
Thus consistency holds and the entire joint observed law, not only selected
moments, remains \(P\).  For every fixed \(d\in I\), compactness of \(I\), the
bound on \(b_u\), and \(\text{ass:observed-integrability}\) imply
\[
 |Y_t^{Q_u}(d)|\leq |Y_t|+K\operatorname{diam}(I),
 \qquad E_{Q_u}|Y_t^{Q_u}(d)|<\infty.
\]
Also, for all \(d,d'\in I\),
\[
 |Y_t^{Q_u}(d)-Y_t^{Q_u}(d')|
 =|b_u|\,|d-d'|
 \leq K|d-d'|,
\]
so each period schedule is individually \(K\)-Lipschitz.

Direct subtraction gives, on one common full-probability event and
simultaneously for every \(d\in I\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)
 &=\Delta Y+b_u(D_1-D_2)\\
 &=\Delta Y-b_uZ\\
 &=\Delta Y-g(X,Z)+u(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Because \(g(X,Z)=E_P[\Delta Y\mid X,Z]\), one may choose conditional-expectation
versions, for every \(d\in I\), satisfying
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X,Z]&=u(X),\\
 E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(d)-Y_1^{Q_u}(d)\mid X]&=u(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
The same two versions work for every \(d\), so the stronger all-\(I\)
simultaneous parallel-trends equality, and hence the required diagonal clause,
holds.  In particular, the second displayed version gives
\(m_{Q_u}(x)=u(x)\) on \(X_0\).  Its level and global Lipschitz restrictions
follow from \(u\in\mathcal C_P\).

The period-two causal movement under this lift is
\[
 Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)
 =b_uZ=g(X,Z)-u(X).
\]
It is integrable because it is bounded in absolute value by \(K|Z|\), and,
being measurable with respect to \((X,Z)\), it satisfies
\[
 \left|E_{Q_u}[Y_2^{Q_u}(D_2)-Y_2^{Q_u}(D_1)\mid X,Z]\right|
 =|b_uZ|\leq K|Z|.
\]
We have therefore checked every member property in
\(\text{def:legal-completion-class}\), so \(Q_u\in\mathfrak Q(P)\).  This also
proves
\(\mathcal C_P\neq\varnothing\Rightarrow\mathfrak Q(P)\neq\varnothing\).
Finally, by the causal definition and iterated expectations,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \theta(Q_u)
 &=\frac{E_P[S\{g(X,Z)-u(X)\}]}{A}\\
 &=\frac{T-J_P(u)}{A},
\end{aligned}
\]
because \(E_P[Sg(X,Z)]=E_P[S\Delta Y]=T\).  Since \(u\) was arbitrary, every
point of \(\Theta(P)\) is attained by a legal full-data law, whereas the first
half of the proof excludes every other value.  This proves both nonemptiness
equivalence and the asserted sharp set equality.

No step used the marginal-quasi-stayer assumption.  The proof instead used the
finite mean-movement bound, the bounded globally Lipschitz trend, the continuous
support version of \(g\), and the simultaneous diagonal clause exactly where
indicated.  These are the extra restrictions built into the sensitivity class
\(\mathfrak Q(P)\).  Accordingly, the set equality just proved is a
characterization of that class and supplies no equality with, or upward
transfer to, the unrestricted published completion class.
body.justification: This is the causal kernel: it replaces an unsupported conditional limit by a two-sided, full-observed-law sharp characterization.
body.gap: Assumption 4 of de Chaisemartin, D'Haultf\oe{}uille, and Vazquez-Bare (2024) imposes only \(P(|\Delta D|\le\eta)>0\), while the Appendix proof of Theorem 1 invokes \(P(|\Delta D|\le\eta\mid D_1)>0\) immediately before display (4). Under the source's parallel-trends condition on the baseline-treatment support, the present theorem gives a sharp sensitivity-class characterization after failure of the published singleton claim. Assumption 5 of de Chaisemartin et al. (arXiv:2201.06898v1, Section 4.1) supplies an analogous baseline-conditional support regime, but its Theorem 3 identifies the unweighted switcher-slope target \(\delta_1\), not WAOSS. Armstrong and Kolesár (2018) motivate the bounded Lipschitz trend as a fixed smoothness restriction, rather than supplying this completion or sharpness argument. Graham and Powell (2012) address irregular correlated-random-coefficient panels and motivate denominator separation, but do not resolve baseline-specific support holes in WAOSS. Freyberger (2017) studies estimation of an upper bound on identified-set diameter, whereas the present result characterizes and attains the full conditional-completion set. Sasaki and Ura (2025) develop bias-corrected point-identified slow-mover limit theory; it is not a competing resolution here because marginal slow changes do not provide the missing baseline-conditional support needed to identify the baseline trend.
body.consumer: Applied continuous-dose DiD analyses with changing temperatures can report a robustness set without imposing a parametric extrapolation across baseline-specific support holes.
